{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/trial.csv')

# Check for duplicates based on patient_id and keep the highest sample_seq
# First, confirm that sample_seq can be used to identify the latest measurement
data_sorted = data.sort_values(by=['patient_id', 'sample_seq'], ascending=[True, False])

# Drop duplicates based on patient_id, keeping the first (highest sample_seq) row
data_deduped = data_sorted.drop_duplicates(subset=['patient_id'], keep='first')

# Verify the deduplication
print(f'Original rows: {len(data)}')
print(f'Deduplicated rows: {len(data_deduped)}')

# Check the distribution of arms and severity to understand the data
print('\nDistribution of arms:')
print(data_deduped['arm'].value_counts())

print('\nDistribution of severity:')
print(data_deduped['severity'].value_counts())

# Filter for CONTROL-arm patients with MODERATE severity
control_moderate = data_deduped[(data_deduped['arm'] == 'control') & (data_deduped['severity'] == 'moderate')]

# Check how many such patients there are
print(f'Number of control-arm, moderate-severity patients: {len(control_moderate)}')

# Compute the fraction who responded
if len(control_moderate) > 0:
    fraction_responded = control_moderate['responded'].mean()
    print(f'Fraction of control-arm, moderate-severity patients who responded: {fraction_responded}')
else:
    print('No control-arm, moderate-severity patients found.')

# Return the fraction
fraction_responded"}
